as_written_in_papers.quote: genetic sequencing revealed a novel frameshift heterozygous mutation (c.764_765insGA) of LAMP2

cases.statement: One heterozygous female proband, aged 25, with cardiac-only disease.

people.label: patient
people.key_phenotypes: LV hypertrophy (IVS up to 16 mm, LVPW 14 mm); ventricular pre-excitation (short PR, delta wave); shock first diagnosed as acute myocarditis; vacuoles and glycogen on myocardial biopsy; normal IQ, EMG and CK

quotes.quote: The proband was a 25-year-old female who complained of intermittent chest distress and shortness of breath for half a month before being admitted to our hospital.
Holter monitor and ECG (Supplementary Figure 1) showed a short PR interval (76 ms), “delta wave,” and lowered ST segment (V4–V6), suggesting preexcitation of the ventricle.

another echocardiogram was performed before discharge and the result still showed a thickened interventricular septum (basal segment: 9 mm; middle segment: 16 mm) and left ventricular posterior wall (11 mm)

The PAS staining showed abnormal cell structure, small vacuoles, and glycogen disposition within muscle fibers (Figures 3A,B), which is consistent with the canonical histological feature of Danon disease.
Intelligence Quotient (IQ) test showed normal results (IQ: 111).

phenotype_specificity.statement: WES on the proband found no other candidate variant in ion-channel or HCM genes. Biopsy showed vacuoles and glycogen. She first presented with shock diagnosed as acute myocarditis, with positive influenza A IgM and other antibody results; the authors say a link to myocarditis is unknown.

quotes.quote: To thoroughly identify the potentially pathogenic gene, whole exome sequencing was carried out using the proband's DNA.
We did not identify any other potentially pathogenic variant of CNVs of known ion channelopathy or hypertrophic cardiomyopathy-related genes.
Respiratory pathogen antibody test showed positive influenza A virus IgM, mycoplasma pneumonia IgG, and chlamydia IgG.

The patient was first diagnosed with acute myocarditis and was treated with mechanical circulatory support measurement (intra-aortic balloon counterpulsation) in accordance with the procedures previously reported because of shock (13).

segregation.statement: Four tested relatives (mother, father, uncle, aunt) are clinically unaffected and do not carry the variant. The 6-year-old brother was neither examined nor tested. No affected relatives.

quotes.quote: However, her mother, father, uncle, and aunt did not have the same mutation (Figure 2A).
Her parents (father, 52 y, and mother, 50 y) did not show any cardiac, skeletal muscle, or mental disorder and neither did her 6-year-old brother.
The patient's family refused echocardiogram and genetic testing for the patient's brother (Figure 2A).

de_novo.statement: Both parents were Sanger-tested and lack the variant; the authors conclude it is de novo. Confirmation of parentage is not reported.

quotes.quote: Validated mutations were also Sanger sequenced in the patient's relatives and extra 800 unrelated Chinese health controls.
The mutation was not identified in her parents or other family members, which suggested this novel frameshift mutation was a de novo one.

functional.statement: Patient material only. Proteomics (LC-MS) of peripheral white blood cells showed lower LAMP2 (normalized to ACTB) than in three healthy controls (supplementary table: 6.4713 vs 37.7–66.5). Myocardial IHC showed patches with high and low LAMP2 expression. No construct assay.

quotes.quote: We performed proteomic analysis to further investigate protein expression caused by this mutation using white blood cells from the patient's peripheral blood.
LAMP2 Expression of the patient was significantly lower than healthy controls (Figure 4D, Supplementary Table 1).
On average, healthy controls express 26.83 ± 12.87 times more LAMP2 than patients carrying c.764_765insGA mutation.
| Symbol | Gene ID | Healthy Control 1 | Healthy Control 2 | Healthy Control 3 | Patient |
Immunohistochemical (IHC) staining of the patient's myocardial slice against LAMP2 showed high and low expressing patches (Figure 4C).

variant_type_and_mechanism.statement: Two-base insertion predicted to cause a frameshift, p.(Asn255LysfsTer29) from the batch HGVS. The paper predicts termination at 281 residues and loss of the transmembrane and cytoplasmic domains, and attributes the female phenotype to haploinsufficiency.

quotes.quote: The c.764_765insGA inserting mutation causes a mistranslation in the downstream and premature termination to 281-amino-acid residues.
The frameshift mutation in our patient caused premature termination of protein translation 46 amino acids forward.
This is probably due to the haploinsufficiency of her heterozygous mutation.

computational_predictions.statement: AlphaFold modelling of the mutant protein, and conservation across species, as the paper states. No scores are given.

quotes.quote: Protein structure remodeling via deep learning technique predicted that the mutation lacks the vital cross membrane domain which may lead to an unstabilized protein structure.
is evolutionary, and highly conserved across multiple species (Figure 2B)

population_data_in_papers.statement: Absent from 800 unrelated Chinese healthy controls and from ExAC, as the paper states.

quotes.quote: Neither was it found in the extra 800 unrelated Chinese healthy controls.
The mutation we revealed was absent in the unrelated 800 healthy controls, the Exome Aggregation Consortium (ExAc), ClinVar, and HGMD databases.

authors_classification.statement: The authors classify it as pathogenic under ACMG, with criteria PVS1+PS2+PM2.

quotes.quote: According to the ACMG guideline and standard, this mutation should be categorized as a pathogenic mutation (PVS1+PS2+PM2).
Through filtering and Sanger sequencing, we found a pathogenic heterozygous frameshift mutation, c.764_765insGA, following the ACMG guideline (14).

concerns: Protein length: the paper says termination 'to 281-amino-acid residues' and also '46 amino acids forward'. The batch HGVS p.(Asn255LysfsTer29) puts the new stop at codon 283. The panel may want to check the paper's numbers against the transcript.
No transcript or protein HGVS is stated in the paper.
The presentation was confounded by acute myocarditis, shock and positive respiratory pathogen serology; LV thickening was re-checked before discharge.
De novo status rests on parental Sanger testing only. Parentage confirmation is not reported, and the brother was not tested.
WES was done on the proband only; relatives had Sanger testing of the variant. The proteomic comparison is one patient against three controls, although the text says 'patients carrying'.
notes_for_panel: Single female proband with parents tested negative, a biopsy consistent with Danon disease and reduced LAMP2 in her white cells. Authors' ACMG codes are quoted under authors_classification only.
